disclaimer.title: Medical Disclaimer
disclaimer.text: This Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) application is an academic research prototype and is NOT intended as a substitute for professional medical judgment, diagnosis, or advice. All AI predictions and dose recommendations must be clinically reviewed. Final pharmacotherapy decisions rest solely with the attending physician (DPJP) and clinical pharmacist.

guide.title: CDSS User Guide
guide.subtitle: Four structured steps to operate CirrhoSmart AI during bedside rounds or inpatient clinical pharmacy medication review.
guide.step1Desc: Choose the module that fits your clinical workflow: AI Mortality Prediction, AI Length of Stay Prediction, or Clinical Dose Recommendation.
guide.step2Desc: Enter the patient's latest clinical and laboratory values. Use the Auto-calculate toggles for CTP, GFR (CKD-EPI 2021), INR, or MAP when constituent parameters are available.
guide.step3Desc: Select the drugs planned for evaluation and mark any accompanying acute complications such as AKI, CKD, HRS, Sepsis/Pneumonia, or Refractory Ascites.
guide.step4Desc: Submit the form for server evaluation. Both predicted probabilities and dosing ranges serve as decision support and require final verification by the DPJP and clinical pharmacist.
guide.offlineTipDesc: CTP scoring, CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR, INR from PT, MAP, and UNOS MELD calculations run locally on your device. Internet connectivity is only required for AI server inference and saving records.

about.title: CirrhoSmart AI
about.subtitle: An evidence-based Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for in-hospital mortality risk stratification, length of stay prediction, and personalized pharmacotherapy dose optimization in hospitalized liver cirrhosis patients.
about.problemsTitle: Bridging Clinical Dilemmas in Cirrhosis Pharmacotherapy
about.problemsIntro: Liver cirrhosis presents complex pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic alterations: impaired hepatic clearance, altered plasma protein binding, portosystemic shunting, and heightened vulnerability to hepatorenal syndrome. In inpatient wards, most regimens require careful dose adjustment to prevent toxicities.
about.problem1Desc: Conventional scoring tools such as CTP and MELD often miss acute decompensating triggers like in-hospital sepsis and rapid renal decline.
about.problem2Desc: Lack of consolidated dosing guidance at the bedside leads to underdosing or toxicity across high-risk drugs (diuretics, beta-blockers, antibiotics).
about.problem3Desc: Clinicians cannot rely on black-box algorithms. CirrhoSmart AI pairs Machine Learning with SHAP interpretability so every prediction can be audited.
about.pillarsTitle: Three Core Modules of CirrhoSmart AI
about.pillarsSubtitle: An interconnected suite of clinical tools built to support attending physicians (DPJP) and hospital clinical pharmacists.
about.pillar1Desc: Random Forest model (AUROC 0.8391) evaluating sepsis, urea, sodium, hepatic encephalopathy, INR, SGOT, GFR, and CTP class with SHAP decomposition.
about.pillar2Desc: Assesses prolonged inpatient stay risk (>7 days median) using 9 multidimensional features and live UNOS MELD integration to guide discharge planning.
about.pillar2Point1: Automatic UNOS MELD calculation (floor 1.0, Cr cap 4.0)
about.pillar2Point2: Linked CKD-EPI 2021 calculation from main labs
about.pillar3Desc: Deterministic rule-based expert system covering 8 cirrhosis-essential drugs/regimens (diuretics, beta-blockers, antibiotics) aligned with AASLD, EASL, and KDIGO.
about.pillar3Point2: Stratified by eGFR, CTP class, MAP, and acute red flags
about.workflowTitle: How CirrhoSmart AI Operates in Inpatient Care
about.workflowSubtitle: Designed for seamless integration into attending physician rounds and clinical pharmacy medication reviews.
about.step1Desc: Enter patient labs or activate local calculators for Child-Turcotte-Pugh score, CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR, INR, and MAP.
about.step2Desc: Server models compute calibrated mortality and prolonged-stay probabilities with SHAP feature attribution.
about.step3Desc: Deterministic rules match each selected medication against CTP, eGFR, MAP, and acute complications for safe dosing ranges.
about.step4Desc: The DPJP and clinical pharmacist verify AI insights and finalize the safest individualized therapeutic plan.
about.teamSubtitle: Multidisciplinary collaboration across Clinical Pharmacy, Hepatology, Pharmacology, and Artificial Intelligence.
about.supportDesc: Have questions regarding this research project, found a technical issue, or interested in clinical collaboration? Send a message to the research team.

methodology.title: Research Methodology & AI Framework
methodology.subtitle: Development and internal validation of an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) model for personalized drug dose recommendations and outcome prediction in hospitalized patients with liver cirrhosis at Dr. M. Djamil General Hospital, Padang.

overview.title: Research Summary & AI Development Pipeline
overview.subtitle: Overview of research rationale, clinical objectives, ethical compliance, and the systematic AI engineering workflow.
overview.urgencyBody: Liver cirrhosis alters drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics via reduced hepatic clearance, portosystemic shunting, hypoalbuminemia, and concomitant renal dysfunction (AKI, CKD, hepatorenal syndrome). Dosing deviations carry high risks of toxicity or therapeutic failure.
overview.solutionBody: CirrhoSmart combines data-driven Machine Learning (Random Forest & XGBoost) for mortality and length-of-stay stratification with a deterministic clinical Rule Engine for medication dosing. Integrated SHAP explanations ensure clinician auditability.
overview.pipelineSubtitle: From retrospective EHR extraction at Dr. M. Djamil Hospital to internal cross-validation and CDSS deployment.
overview.step1Desc: 583 adult patients with confirmed cirrhosis (ICD-10 K74.6) across 137 clinical & laboratory variables.
overview.step2Desc: Random Forest Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE), outlier handling, feature scaling, and dynamic MELD computation.
overview.step3Desc: Random Forest & XGBoost trained on Mortality (n=395) and LoS (n=583) using Repeated Stratified 5-Fold CV.
overview.step4Desc: SHAP TreeExplainer attribution paired with deterministic dosing rules across 8 medications per AASLD/EASL/KDIGO.
overview.ethicsBody: This study was approved by the Health Research Ethics Committee (KEPK) of Dr. M. Djamil General Hospital, Padang on 22 July 2025 (Reference Number: DP.04.03/D.XVI.2.3/1027/2025). All patient data was de-identified in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

cohort.title: Baseline Cohort Characteristics (Table 1)
cohort.subtitle: Distribution of demographic characteristics, hepatic severity, portal hypertension complications, and comorbidities across 583 patients.
cohort.observationBody: Child-Turcotte-Pugh Class B (56.1%) and Class C (31.4%) comprised 87.5% of the cohort, reflecting advanced baseline dysfunction. Frequent portal hypertension complications (varices 36.6%, ascites 33.3%, HE 19.4%) and extrahepatic comorbidities (pneumonia 21.5%, CKD 17.4%) require multifactorial dosage adjustment.

hybridAi.title: Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Architecture
hybridAi.subtitle: Synergistic integration of probabilistic Machine Learning and deterministic clinical rule reasoning.
hybridAi.mlBody: Responsible for quantitative risk projection, outputting calibrated probabilities for in-hospital mortality and prolonged hospitalization (> 7 days).
hybridAi.mlPoint3: Integrated TreeExplainer for SHAP feature decomposition
hybridAi.ruleBody: Translates AASLD, EASL, KDIGO, and FDA guidance into individualized dose recommendations without generative AI hallucination risk.
hybridAi.rulePoint1: Multi-axis triage: CTP class, eGFR, MAP, and body weight
hybridAi.rulePoint2: Critical safety overrides for AKI, Sepsis, HRS, and AST/ALT
hybridAi.prep1Body: Handles missing values via Random Forest MICE to preserve non-linear biological relationships instead of simplistic mean imputation.
hybridAi.prep2Body: Calculated dynamically: 3.78×ln(bil) + 11.2×ln(INR) + 9.57×ln(Cr) + 6.43, with 1.0 floor and creatinine capped at 4.0 mg/dL.
hybridAi.prep3Body: Continuous lab parameters standardized via StandardScaler and categorical indicators transformed via One-Hot Encoding inside CV folds.

metrics.title: Model Performance Comparison (Table 3)
metrics.subtitle: Internal 5-fold cross-validation results comparing Random Forest vs. XGBoost across mortality and length of stay.
metrics.interpretation1: 1. Mortality Prediction: Both models achieved strong discrimination (RF AUROC 0.8391; XGBoost 0.8371), confirming baseline labs and acute complications reliably stratify inpatient mortality risk.
metrics.interpretation2: 2. Length of Stay (LoS) Prediction: Discrimination was modest (RF AUROC 0.5664; XGBoost 0.5005) due to dynamic hospitalization logistics and 'survival bias' among critically ill early mortalities.

shap.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (SHAP)
shap.subtitle: Deconstructing model predictions into individualized feature contributions using SHapley Additive exPlanations.
shap.mortalitySub: Features ranked by mean absolute SHAP value (|SHAP|):
shap.mortality1Desc: Strongest binary risk drivers; presence of either markedly elevates predicted inpatient death probability.
shap.mortality2Desc: Elevated values correlate monotonically with higher mortality risk (coagulopathy & hepatocellular injury).
shap.mortality3Desc: Severe hyponatremia (<130 mmol/L) and renal impairment (eGFR <30) signal heightened hepatorenal syndrome risk.
shap.mortality4Desc: Consistent monotonic severity gradient: Class C > Class B > Class A.
shap.losSub: Features ranked by mean absolute SHAP value (|SHAP|):
shap.los1Desc: Inverse relation: lower bilirubin linked with longer stay due to early-death survival bias.
shap.los2Desc: Renal dysfunction and active hepatic inflammation prolong inpatient stabilization duration.
shap.los3Desc: Moderate contributors reflecting systemic physiological stress and patient reserves.
shap.los4Desc: Minimal independent influence on length of stay alone.
shap.casePatientTitle: Patient Profile: 64 yo, CTP Class B, MELD 17, Active Sepsis & Hepatic Encephalopathy
shap.caseBody: Labs: Urea 96 mg/dL, eGFR 26 mL/min/1.73m², Bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL, Creatinine 2.7 mg/dL, INR 1.11, AST 70 U/L, Sodium 136 mmol/L. Predicted mortality probability reached 0.697 (vs. 0.499 cohort baseline).

dosing.title: Dose Evaluation System & Clinical Concordance
dosing.subtitle: Cohort appropriateness distribution across drug classes and concordance validation against specialist clinical adjudication.
